title: Beowulf (Cotton MS Vitellius A.xv)
shelf_note: A facsimile of the Beowulf manuscript (Cotton Vitellius A.xv); this leaf holds lines 827–849, the end of fitt XII and the opening of fitt XIII.
structure_note: 32 backsteps and 30 repeats come from the several competing foliations on each leaf: this leaf shows 148, 151 and 153 in different hands. This is not a splice.

pages.not_this_leaf_evidence: The first line is stored as 'mīne þeode se þe ellen mærþo', but the clearly legible leaf reads '[ni]hte weorce gefeh ellen mærþum' (Beowulf 827: rejoiced in his night-work). The stored words are not on the leaf, and the translation renders them as 'my people, he who had attained the glory of courage'.

The second half (fitt XIII) is close.

title: Vitae et sententiae philosophorum. Tr: Ambrosius Traversarius
shelf_note: Traversari's Latin Diogenes Laertius, 1472 incunable (BAV Inc.III.83); the page is from Book III (Plato's divisions).
rights_flag: The scan carries a burned-in diagonal watermark 'ALL RIGHTS RESERVED © Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana' and the footer 'Copyright © Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana'. This is a digitisation licence on a 1472 book, not a modern edition, but the reuse terms should be checked.
structure_note: 39 backsteps and 31 repeats among 172 'printed' numbers. An incunable has no printed pagination; these are pencilled leaf numbers and misreads, not a splice.
